Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph s. 2021 OPINION NO cg HON. EMMANUEL ANTONIO M. UMALI Vice Governor Province of Nueva Ecija Office of the Vice-Governor 2nd Floor, New Capitol Bldg., Brgy. Singalat, Palayan City, Nueva Ecija Dear Vice Gov. Umali: This refers to your letter dated 30 May 2024 with the subject "Designation Order of Hon. Jason Abalos as Acting Vice Governor of Nueva Ecija". Per the representation, the issue centers on the implementation of the Order of the Office of the Ombudsman dated 10 May 2024 ("Order" for brevity) in OMB-C-A-APR- 24-0029 entitled "ROBERTO M. DULDULAO VS. AURELIO M. UMALI, ET AL", placing Nueva Ecija Govemor Aurelio M. Umali under PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION until the administrative adjudication of the case is terminated, but not to exceed SIX (6) MONTHS, vis-å-vis the subsequent issuance of a temporary restraining order ("TRO", for brevity) by the Court of Appeals, enjoining or prohibiting its implementation. Before delving into the discussion, allow us to begin by stating the pertinent factual antecedents surrounding the implementation of the Order based on the Certification / Compliance Report of our Regional Office in Region Ill, which was submitted to the Office of the Ombudsman on 23 May 2024: 1. On 22 May 2024, around 10:28 a.m., a copy of the Order was tendered to Atty. Olive Jean Manuel-Comejo, Acting Provincial Assessor, at the Office of the Provincial Governor, Provincial Capitol, Gabaldon St. 3100, Cabanatuan, Nueva Ecija; 2. On 22 May 2024, at around 11:41 a.m.-11:42a.m. of the same date, proceeded to post the copy of the Order on the front door of the Office of the at the Office of the Provincial Governor, Provincial Capitol, Gabaldon St. 3100, Cabanatuan, Nueva Ecija; 3. Then, at 12:44 p.m., a copy of the Order was posted on the entrance door of the New Provincial Capitol, Palaya City, Nueva Ecija It is important to note that the said modes of service were resorted to due to the absence of respondent Governor Aurelio M. Umali in both offices and the refusal of his representatives to receive the Order. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

It is noteworthy that a Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) enjoining or prohibiting the implementation of the Order was issued on the same day, 22 May 2024, by the Court of Appeals after the Ombudsman Decision was already implemented by the concerned DILG Regional Office. Premised from the foregoing arose the request for definitive guidance on the following queries: a. Is there a "temporary vacancy" in the Office of the Govemor even though the implementation of the order of preventive suspension was enjoined by the Court of Appeals, pursuant to the temporary restraining order issued on C.S.-G.R. SP No. 184192, on 22 May 2024? b. Is the undersigned Vice Governor being mandated and ordered by the DILG to assume the functions and duties of Acting Govemor, notwithstanding the said Temporary Restraining Order dated 22 May 2024 and Resolution dated 27 May 2024? c. Should the undersigned Vice Governor and Hon. Jason Abalos obey and follow the said Temporary Restraining Order dated 22 May 2024 and Resolution dated 27 May 2024? a. Is there a "temporary vacancy" in the Office of the Governor even though the implementation of the order of preventive suspension was enjoined by the Court of Appeals, pursuant to the temporary restraining order issued on C.S.-G.R. SP No. 184192, on 22 May 2024? As stated in the above narration of facts, the Order was already fully implemented before the issuance of the TRO. The Order was duly implemented as early as the moming of 22 May 2024, while the TRO was issued only in the aftemoon. In this regard, we highlight the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of "The City Government of Caloocan v. Carmel Development Inc. " (G.R. No. 240255, 25 January 2023) pertaining to the doctrine of fait accompli in relation to TRO / injunction order, viz.: [Tlhe Court has repeatedly held that when the act sought to be enjoined has become fait accompli, the prayer for preliminary injunction should be denied. Indeed, when the events sought to be prevented by injunction or prohibition had already happened, nothing more could be enjoined or prohibited. An injunction will not issue to restrain the performance of an act already done. Evidently, we are of the considered view that since the act sought to be restrained had already occurred, i.e. the implementation of the Ombudsman's Order for Preventive Suspension, there is nothing more that can be enjoined by the TRO. In other words, the implementation of the Ombudsman's Suspension Order rendered moot the TRO issued in favor of the petitioner. Page 2 of 4

Thus, it is our opinion that a temporary vacancy exists in the Office of the Governor as a result of the preventive suspensions imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman and implemented by this Department. b. Is the undersigned Vice Governor being mandated and ordered by the DILG to assume the functions and duties of Acting Governor, notwithstanding the said Temporary Restraining Order dated 22 May 2024 and Resolution dated 27 May 2024? c. Should the undersigned Vice Governor and Hon. Jason Abalos obey and follow the said Temporary Restraining Order dated 22 May 2024 and Resolution dated 27 May 2024? Considering that the queries are interrelated, we deem it proper to answer them collectively. Under Sec. 46 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", as amended ("LGC", for brevity), when the governor is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for legal reasons (suspension from office), the vice- governor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the provincial governor. Accordingly, Sec. 46 of the LGC is explicit, and necessitates that you, as the Vice Governor, shall perform the duties and functions of Acting Governor, by operation of law, immediately after the implementation of the Order. Correspondingly, anent your automatic assumption to office as Acting Provincial Governor of Nueva Ecija, to fill in the vacancy in the said office and further prevent hiatus in, and paralysis of local government operations, and ensure the uninterrupted delivery of basic services to the constituents of the province of Nueva Ecija, the application of Administrative Order No. 15 s. 2018 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 is necessary. Item lv (B) of DILG MC 2019-21 states: B. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Provincial Vice Governor, City Vice Mayor and Municipal Vice Mayor There is a temporary vacancy in the office of the vice-govemor, city or municipal vice mayor, if he/she is temporarily incapacitated to perform his/her duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. 1. When a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the provincial vice governor or city or municipality vice mayor, the highest ranking sangguniang panlalawigan/panlungsod/bayan member, as the case may be, shall be designated by the President, through the SILG or the OIC-DILG immediately upon the report of the concerned DILG Regional Office of the said vacancy, as acting provincial vice governor or city or municipality vice mayor. Page 3 of 4

He/She shall exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the office, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss officials and employees in the sangguniang panlalawigan/panlungsod/bayan which can only be exercised if the temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. In view of the foregoing, this Office issued a Designation Order to the highest ranking Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, Hon. JASON ABALOS to assume as Acting Vice Governor during the period of vacancy caused by your temporary assumption to the office of the Governor. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY TH THORITY OF THE SECR VICTOR . LLAMAS Underse e ryfor Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/rjki COPY FURNISHED: ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG-Region Ill Page 4 of 4
